item.title: Said & Checked, Economy and Jobs, 2026-11-21: none false or contradicted, 1 unsettled (Chuck Grassley)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Chuck Grassley, U.S. Senator: “In July of 2026, a brief published by the Administration for Children and Families detailed that many families receiving TANF are not actually engaged in work or work activities.” Unsettled. ACF published a TANF brief on July 20, 2026 on the caseload reduction credit, but only its landing page could be read, not the brief's text; a June 29, 2026 ACF brief is the one reported to find that most work-eligible families logged no work hours, and its text could not be read directly either. Whether the July brief says many families are not engaged in work is not decided.

item.title: Said & Checked, Economy and Jobs, 2026-11-20: 1 contradicted (David Schweikert)
item.description:
False or contradicted

  • David Schweikert, U.S. Representative: “How about an 8 percent wealth tax? This is a good one. We get basically one-half a percent of GDP.” Contradicted. Saez and Zucman's estimate of Sen. Sanders's 2019 wealth tax, which tops out at 8% on wealth over $10 billion, is $4.35 trillion over a decade, about 1.6% of GDP a year, roughly three times the stated figure. What remains open is whether a different 8% design or scorer was meant; other scores of the plan were not read in full.

item.title: Said & Checked, Economy and Jobs, 2026-11-18: none false or contradicted, 4 unsettled (Tim Walberg, Bruce Westerman, James Clyburn)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Tim Walberg, U.S. Representative from Michigan: “Fishing in the Great Lakes alone contributes more than $5 billion to the regional economy and supports over 75,000 jobs.” Unsettled. A Great Lakes Fishery Commission study puts recreational fishing's economic output at $5.1 billion (reported by Michigan Public), matching the dollar figure. The commission's factsheet reportedly counts about 35,800 recreational and nearly 3,000 commercial jobs, about 39,000 in all, short of 75,000; that factsheet could not be read directly, so the jobs figure is not settled here.
  • Bruce Westerman, U.S. Representative from Arkansas: “sawmills and paper mills are closing all across the country, our Nation's forests are going up in flames.” Unsettled. AskAmerica's wildfire perimeter data show 2.2 million to 8.6 million acres burned a year in 2020-2025 and 8.3 million so far in 2026, across 4,000 to 8,000 mapped fires a year. No count of sawmill or paper mill closures was found, and 'all across the country' is a loose quantifier.
  • James Clyburn, U.S. Representative from South Carolina: “Today, our primary industries are transportation and tourism, and the fastest growing segment of tourism is heritage tourism.” Unsettled. No source was found that ranks South Carolina's industries in a way that settles 'primary industries' or that names heritage tourism as tourism's fastest-growing segment; the warehouse has no tourism tables, and the state tourism agency's research pages were not read.
